subject: Warsh speech resolves toward conditional tightening; market reprices September hike odds
body_md: Thesis: The prior Jackson Hole state `LIVE_POLICY_SIGNAL / DIRECTION_NOT_YET_RESOLVED` should be superseded by `CONDITIONAL_TIGHTENING_BIAS + DATA_DEPENDENT_TIMING`. Primary Fed text says the 2% PCE target is firm/fixed, inflation is not necessarily self-correcting, short-term rates are the predominant dual-mandate tool, current credit/loan markets show few signs of policy restraint, and the Fed has 'work to do' unless underlying inflation moves clearly and sufficiently quickly toward target. Independent market corroboration: Reuters reports September hike odds moved to roughly even from ~40% earlier Friday and the 2-year Treasury yield rose to a one-month high. This is not an unconditional hike call: Warsh explicitly rejects forward guidance and commits to a discipline, not a decision. Second-order implication: the AI capex boom itself enters the reaction function as both a productivity/growth force and a source of resilient demand/financial conditions; Nexus should model AI capex -> growth/financial conditions -> policy restraint need rather than treating AI and macro as separate graphs. Evidence: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/warsh20260828a.htm ; https://www.reuters.com/business/will-warshs-jackson-hole-speech-be-course-correction-or-detour-2026-08-28/ . Contradiction: incoming August labor/inflation data could weaken materially, energy/geopolitical pressures could recede, or financial conditions could tighten on their own. Conviction: +0.91. What would falsify this: subsequent Fed communication explicitly leaning toward easing/holding despite persistent inflation, a material deterioration in labor/growth data that changes the reaction function, or market pricing fully reversing the post-speech tightening repricing after digesting the complete speech.
